headline: High: Copilot can read and modify repo/editor context while Botpress is an unverified open-source chatbot with no documented isolation, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support chatbot with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while GitHub Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context by default. That creates a plausible path where Botpress-generated content is copied into code or prompts that Copilot then treats as trusted input. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are pasted into editor buffers or repo files consumed by Copilot
IF Copilot Workspace or chat is used on content originating from Botpress
mitigations: Keep Botpress outputs out of code comments and prompt files
Require human review before copying Botpress text into Copilot-visible files
Use separate workspaces for chatbot content and coding tasks
Add a prompt-injection warning banner in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between chatbot and IDE

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is open-source and shows no filesystem or network surfaces, but Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive data enters the shared repo or buffers, Copilot can transmit it to a vendor backend. Because Botpress has no documented data-handling surface, the pairwise leakage path is indirect but real in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive text from Botpress conversations is stored in files or buffers visible to Copilot
IF Copilot is used with repo context containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Do not place secrets or regulated text in shared repo files
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Copilot
Redact Botpress transcripts before saving them
Review Copilot context files before enabling chat
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on editor buffers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress has package-install capability, while Copilot can write files and modify git state. Even though Botpress lacks documented filesystem write, the pair still overlaps on code-bearing workflows: Copilot can edit repo state that Botpress-generated instructions may influence. Uncertainty about Botpress write surfaces prevents a lower rating, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated instructions are used to drive edits in the same repository Copilot modifies
IF multiple Copilot instances or editors touch the same git branch
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch
Require lockstep human approval for git writes
Avoid letting Botpress generate patch text for Copilot to apply
Check for concurrent editor sessions before editing
requires-engineering: add repository locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace plans and applies edits, and its chat/completions can turn upstream text into code changes. Botpress is a chatbot that can emit unverified instructions or facts. When Copilot treats Botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into committed code or applied edits. The default edit-assist workflow makes this dangerous enough for high severity.
conditions: IF Botpress output is used as the source text for Copilot Workspace or chat
IF Copilot applies edits based on Botpress-generated claims without independent verification
mitigations: Require source verification before applying Copilot edits
Keep Botpress outputs out of task specs
Use a second reviewer for any Copilot-generated patch
Limit Copilot to autocomplete-only mode for sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add citation checks before edit application

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo OAuth and vendor-only egress, while Botpress is open-source with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That mismatch can create compliance gaps for regulated code or transcripts if Botpress content is moved into Copilot-visible files. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined workflow.
conditions: IF regulated data from Botpress is stored in repositories or buffers accessible to Copilot
IF organizational policy requires residency or retention controls not documented for this pair
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot-visible repositories
Document retention and residency expectations for both tools
Use separate projects for regulated and non-regulated work
Review GitHub OAuth scope usage before deployment
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and formal compliance review
